late.text: Your project is late. The deliverables are not ready. Should you add more people?

channels.text: Every pair of people on a team needs a communication channel. With N people, there are N times N minus one, over two channels.

grow.text: Three people: three channels. Four people: six. Five people: ten. Eight people: twenty-eight.

brooks.text: Fred Brooks, in The Mythical Man-Month: adding people to a failing project makes matters worse.

why.text: The cost of more communication can outweigh the gain from dividing the work.

size.text: So teams stay small. The slides give optimal sizes between three and nine people. A scrum team: three to nine, usually with two to five developers.

org.text: Teams also sit inside an organization, in one of three structures.

proj.text: Project-oriented: each person is dedicated to one project. Performance and schedules improve, but engineers are isolated, and reuse goes down.

func.text: Function-oriented: groups by function, and functional managers act as project managers. Clear decisions, but moving people between projects causes delay.

matrix.text: Matrix: people belong to a functional group, but are loaned to projects for their expertise. The main advantage: efficient use of resources.
